map.基于身高、体重与红细胞压积变化，估算血容量与产后出血量，辅助临床分级。: Estimate blood volume and postpartum blood loss from height, weight and hematocrit change to support clinical grading.

map.出血量 = 血容量 × (Hct前 − Hct后) / Hct前: Blood loss = blood volume × (pre-Hct − post-Hct) / pre-Hct
map.💡 估算公式：血容量（Nadler 公式）= 0.3561 × H³(m) +: 💡 Formula: blood volume (Nadler) = 0.3561 × H³(m) + 0.03308 × W(kg) + 0.1833; blood loss = blood volume × (pre-Hct − post-Hct) / pre-Hct.
map.PPH 分级：阴道分娩失血 ≥500mL，剖宫产 ≥1000mL；严重 PPH: PPH grading: vaginal loss ≥500 mL, cesarean ≥1000 mL; severe PPH >1500 mL.
map.产前/产后 Hct 需为同一时间窗可比的静脉血结果。: Pre- and post-delivery Hct must be comparable venous samples from the same time window.
map.本工具为估算辅助，不能替代临床评估与实验室检查。: This tool is an estimation aid and cannot replace clinical assessment and lab tests.
map.📚 深度解析：产后失血量估算（红细胞压积法）: 📚 In-Depth: Postpartum Blood Loss Estimation (Hematocrit Method)
map.产后用产前产后 Hct 变化反推实际失血量，比目测更准确。: Postpartum, infer actual loss from pre/post Hct change—more accurate than visual estimate.
map.隐性出血（宫腔积血）时用血色素/Hct 下降估算。: For occult bleeding (retained clot), estimate from hemoglobin/Hct drop.
map.大量输血方案启动前量化失血程度。: Quantify blood loss before activating a massive transfusion protocol.
map.产妇血容量约 5000mL，产前 Hct 35%、产后降至 25%：失血量 =: Maternal blood volume ~5000 mL, pre-Hct 35% to post 25%: loss = 5000 × (35−25) ÷ 35 ≈ 1428.6 mL, ≥1000 mL is severe PPH needing active management.
map.Hct 由 38% 降至 34%：失血量 = 5000 × (38−34) ÷: Hct 38% to 34%: loss = 5000 × (38−34) ÷ 38 ≈ 526.3 mL, just over 500 mL; start monitoring and uterotonics per PPH protocol.
map.为什么用 Hct 反推而不直接称纱布？: Why infer from Hct instead of weighing swabs?
map.目测和称重会低估隐性失血（尤其宫腔内积血），Hct 法反映整体红细胞丢失，更适合: Visual and weighing methods underestimate occult loss (especially intrauterine clot); the Hct method reflects overall red-cell loss and better shows whether the transfusion threshold is reached.
map.正常产后失血上限是多少？: What is the normal upper limit of postpartum loss?
map.阴道分娩 ≥500mL、剖宫产 ≥1000mL 即诊断产后出血；≥1500mL: Vaginal ≥500 mL or cesarean ≥1000 mL defines PPH; ≥1500 mL is refractory, needing massive transfusion and surgical intervention.
